publications.title: Machine-learning Prediction of Type-III Instabilities and Spontaneous Energy Localization
publications.subtitle: Journal of Applied Nonlinear Dynamics
publications.description: Modulational instability of a plane-wave mode is known to lead to spontaneous energy localization in nonlinear lattices without the presence of impurities. Where the energy dynamically localizes in the system is highly sensitive to initial conditions. Here we numerically investigate sine-Gordon-type lattices and first show that spatial smoothing of the observed dynamical variables on the lattice can already substantially improve predictions of the eventual localization site from early-time data traces alone, suggesting that the type-III instability that forms the energy hotspot is sensitive to energetic clusters. We then show that machine learning leads to additional dramatic improvement in prediction accuracy. Finally, we also examine the role of chain impurities in determining the localization site.

It has been three weeks into my internship at COUNTRY Financial® ’s DigitaLab, and one thing has become very clear: engineering and implementing AI products is about much more than models. Over the past few weeks, I’ve had the opportunity to work across several AI and data engineering concepts and apply it to real-world production projects. These include developing and implementing LLM memory architectures, API endpoints to MCP integrations, designing LLM evaluation frameworks, and creating more human-centered AI experiences. Every project has provided a new perspective on what it takes to build intelligent systems that are not only capable, but actually useful. What has stood out most is how collaborative the process is. The most gratifying aspect of the process has been getting to work alongside a highly capable team. With each assignment, we have had to deconstruct challenging situations, share responsibility for tasks, leverage each other's strengths, and align as we refine our ideas. The whole process has helped me gain a greater understanding of project management and communication, as well as the importance of trust within a team environment. Outside of the projects, some of the highlights of my experience thus far include the people that I've had the pleasure of meeting. From amazing interns to professionals, there have been a lot of people who exhibit such enthusiasm and excitement while helping others learn. I am happy to have built friendships over the past three weeks. Excited to keep learning, keep building, and put these experiences into action at the upcoming COUNTRY Financial Hackathon. Looking forward to what the rest of the summer has in store.

As the academic year comes to a close, I'm excited to share that I'll be transferring to the University of Chicago this fall. My past year at UCSB has been deeply meaningful and rewarding, and I’m grateful for everyone who supported me along the way. Stoked for the journey ahead!

A huge thank you to Lauren Somerhalder for guiding us through our first week and giving us interns a space to bond as a team! Thank you to my manager Sri Adusumilli, Nick Schulz, and Kozue S. for answering my ceaseless stream of questions. I look forward to many more lessons learned as I contribute to the team!
